findings.title: Two-caller receipt exercises the pre-claim existence check, not the atomic mkdir gate
findings.requirement: Brief criterion 9 and the wrapper's own contract that one authorization can never start two exports. The only gate that is race-safe when two callers pass the pre-check in the same instant is `mkdir "$OUT/claim.d"`.
findings.scenario: Two callers start close together but not simultaneously: the second reaches the pre-claim `for f in claim.d invocation-log.jsonl ...` loop after the first has already created claim.d, so it is refused there. If instead both callers passed that loop in the same instant, only the atomic mkdir would separate them - and that path has no receipt in the packet, while coverage.md's Limits paragraph does not say so.
findings.falsifying_observation: Caller B's captured output is exactly `PRECONDITION an invocation was already started (claim.d exists)`. That string is emitted only by the pre-claim existence loop; the mkdir failure branch emits `claim refused: an existing claim or an unwritable record directory`. Both exit 97, so the [0,97] status pair cannot distinguish them.
findings.correction: Add one sentence to coverage.md Limits: the two-caller receipt demonstrates single-claim behaviour through the pre-claim existence check, and the atomic mkdir window is argued from the frozen wrapper text rather than observed. No code change.

findings.title: Empty complement is undisclosed, so membership `unsupported: 0` can read as a passed off-pool control
findings.location: coverage.md:36-38; the `membership` observation in rehearsal/result.json; governing/brief.md acceptance criteria 4 and 8
findings.requirement: Brief criterion 4: "Unsupported root keys equal the complement of H within the declared board." Brief criterion 8: an off-pool hand must default, discriminated from an in-pool CHECK hit by its retained reason.
findings.scenario: A controller or later drafter reads coverage.md's line "1,081 hits, no disagreement/unsupported; exact entries" as evidence that the off-pool default path was exercised and passed, and carries that into the agreement phase's coverage claim - when in fact no off-pool default was ever taken in this phase.
findings.falsifying_observation: With coverage = declared-full, H is the entire 1081-hand universe, so the complement within the declared board is empty by construction. I recomputed the raw membership rows: all 1081 rows are classification=hit with provider_reason=blueprint_hit and table_hit true; the `blueprint_default` branch of eval_bridge.validate_membership is never taken, and `unsupported` is 0 because the set is empty, not because a control passed. completion.complete builds control-off-pool.json only for phase 'agreement'.
findings.correction: One sentence in coverage.md: for declared-full the complement of H is empty, so criterion 4's complement clause holds vacuously here and criterion 8's off-pool default control is deferred to agreement's test-only proper-subset artifact.

findings.title: Four attribution-helper refusal branches are unexercised and not named in the coverage limits
findings.requirement: The packet's own claim that attribution "binds exact new bytes", and the handoff's rule that meaningful assertions be recomputed rather than accepted as passing labels.
findings.scenario: A retained run produces a journal row whose `output` is absent or non-string, whose row is unparsable, whose output file is missing, or whose `runtimes_sha256` does not match the sibling runtimes.json. Those refusal branches would fire for the first time in production, with no synthetic receipt behind them. The runtimes branch is the most reachable, because finish_run always writes runtimes_sha256 when an output directory is set, so the real retained row will carry it while only the passing side has ever been exercised.
findings.falsifying_observation: The six synthetic helper cases cover ABSENT(3), EXTRA(4), MISMATCH source_commit(5), MISMATCH output_sha256(5), BOUND(0) and BOUND over CRLF(0). No case produces `MISMATCH unparsable-row`, `MISMATCH output-missing`, `MISMATCH output-file-missing` or `MISMATCH runtimes_sha256`; none of the synthetic rows even contains a runtimes_sha256 field. coverage.md's Limits paragraph names filesystem errors, interrupted cleanup and unrelated journal writers, but not these branches.
findings.correction: Add the four synthetic cases to focused-checks.py, or name them explicitly in coverage.md Limits. (All four are conservative refusals that can only clear EVIDENCE, so no false success is reachable through them - hence Minor.)

findings.title: A post-claim `set -u` expansion can consume the one-shot claim without launching
findings.location: invoke.sh launch block: `env -i SystemRoot="${SystemRoot:-$SYSTEMROOT}" TEMP="$TEMP" TMP="$TMP" ...`, executed after `mkdir "$OUT/claim.d"` and both record writes; authorization-request.md:53-55
findings.requirement: The wrapper's stated contract that a refusal before acquisition consumes nothing, together with the one-shot nature of the controller's authorization.
findings.scenario: An operator runs the authorized wrapper from a shell in which both SystemRoot and SYSTEMROOT are absent (or TEMP or TMP is absent). Under `set -u` the parameter expansion aborts the shell before `env -i` runs, so the outcome is: claim taken, claim record and start record written, no child launched, no end record, no PHASE or DONE line, exit status 1. Nothing is falsely reported as successful, but the single authorized attempt is consumed and only the controller can resolve the abandoned claim.
findings.falsifying_observation: The construct sits below the claim in invoke.sh, and `set -u -o pipefail` is in force from the top of the script; there is no guard on those three variables anywhere above the claim. authorization-request.md's operator instructions specify `Bash --noprofile --norc`, REHEARSAL unset and no root overrides, but name no required environment variables. Both branches are demonstrably satisfied on this machine: the r004 solve launched through the same construct, and this packet's rehearsal exercised the `$SYSTEMROOT` fallback because Python upper-cases environment keys on Windows.
findings.correction: Documentation only: list SystemRoot/SYSTEMROOT, TEMP and TMP as required environment in authorization-request.md's operator instructions. Moving the expansion above the claim would change the frozen wrapper digest and re-open the freeze for a hazard that has not occurred.
